newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Bulatovic loses power struggle in Montenegro.
newsitem.headline: Bulatovic loses power struggle in Montenegro.

text.p: Montenegro's ruling DPS party nominated Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic as its candidate for the Yugoslav republic's presidency on Friday, after withdrawing support from current President Momir Bulatovic.
Bulatovic, voted out of the DPS leadership, split the party in two when he walked out taking a third of the main board membership with him.
Djukanovic and Bulatovic have been locked in a running feud over the 35-year-old prime minister's hostility to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
Presidential elections which Bulatovic is expected to contest as an independent or at the head of a new party are due to be held in Montenegro by November.

Former Montenegrin culture minister Goran Rakocevic told Belgrade's Radio Index that the split could lead to Montenegro's rejection of support for Milosevic's expected bid to become president of Federal Yugoslavia, which comprises only Serbia and Monetenegro.
Djukanovic accused Milosevic of slowing Montenegro's economic development by refusing cooperation with the international community since the lifting of U.N. sanctions against Yugoslavia.
Montenegro has equal status with Serbia in the federation despite being a fraction of its size in terms of population and its economy.
